Patient: I'm 72 years old, and I'm a woman. I'm here for a follow-up on my hypertension, and I also wanted to talk about the shot you mentioned last time for helping with my drinking.
Doctor: Could you clarify what you meant by 'the shot' for managing your drinking? Additionally, could you provide more details about your hypertension, such as when you were diagnosed and any medications you are currently taking?
Patient: The shot is for helping me stop drinking, something we talked about last time. As for my hypertension, I was diagnosed a while back, and I'm currently taking hydrochlorothiazide 12.5 mg once daily and half a dose of lisinopril 20 mg, because when I first took the full dose, I felt really tired and had some headaches and a swooshing sound in my left ear. I've been checking my blood pressure at home, and it's been fluctuating, usually higher in the evenings but lower in the mornings.
Doctor: Could you provide more details about your blood pressure readings, including the specific values you've been recording at home and the time of day they were taken?
Patient: Sure. In the mornings, my blood pressure is generally lower, around 130 to 145 over 95 to 100. But in the evenings, it tends to be higher, sometimes up to 150 over 100. I noticed that if I sit for a while before taking it, it goes down a bit, like when I come in here for my appointment. I take my medications in the morning, which is why my morning numbers seem more normal.
Doctor: Could you clarify what you mean by 'the shot' and whether you have previously received any interventions or medications for alcohol use disorder?
Patient: The shot is something we talked about last time for helping me stop drinking. I think it's called naltrexone, and I believe the other name is Vivitrol. I may have taken the pill form before, but I'm more comfortable with the shot because I know I won't forget to take it.
Doctor: Has the patient ever experienced any adverse effects or lack of efficacy with naltrexone in pill form? If so, what were they?
Patient: I don't remember exactly, but I know that when I took it as a pill, I didn't stick with it because I kept missing doses. With the shot, I feel more confident I'll get it, so I'm hoping it works better for me this time.
Doctor: Could you provide more details about your alcohol use patterns, including frequency, quantity, and any specific triggers or attempts at reducing consumption prior to considering naltrexone/Vivitrol?
Patient: I've been drinking hard alcohol four to five times a week for a while. I've tried to cut back on my own, but it's been really hard. I know I need to stop, especially because it's affecting my blood pressure, but I struggle with the urge to drink. That's why I'm hoping the shot will help me with that.
Doctor: Could you please provide more details about your alcohol use patterns, including the typical amount consumed per session, the type of alcohol, and any specific triggers or situations that lead to drinking?
Patient: I usually drink hard alcohol, like whiskey or vodka, and I'll have four or five drinks each time I drink. I don't really have specific triggers, but it's just something I've been doing for a while, and it's really hard to stop on my own. I know it's not good for me, especially with my blood pressure, which is why I'm trying to get help with the shot.
Doctor: Could you please share more about how long you have been drinking alcohol regularly and whether you have experienced any specific symptoms or issues related to your alcohol use, such as nausea, tremors, or difficulty sleeping?
Patient: I've been drinking regularly for a long time, maybe even years. I haven't had any big issues like tremors or nausea from it, but I do know it's been affecting my blood pressure. I just feel like I need to stop, and I'm hoping the shot will help me with that.
Doctor: Can you provide more details about the frequency, quantity, and duration of your alcohol use, as well as any specific patterns or triggers that have been associated with your drinking?
Patient: I've been drinking hard alcohol, like whiskey or vodka, four to five times a week for a while. I usually have four or five drinks each time, and it's just something I've been doing for a long time. I don't really have specific triggers, but it's really hard to stop on my own. I know it's not good for me, especially with my blood pressure, which is why I'm trying to get help with the shot.
Doctor: How long has the patient been drinking alcohol at this frequency and quantity, and has she experienced any withdrawal symptoms or cravings when attempting to cut back?
Patient: I've been drinking this way for a long time, maybe even years. I haven't had any big withdrawal symptoms when I've tried to cut back, but I do have a strong urge to drink, especially when I'm stressed or just going through my day. That's why I'm hoping the shot will help me with the cravings.
Doctor: Has the patient experienced any adverse effects or noticed any changes in her alcohol consumption patterns since starting naltrexone in pill form?
Patient: I think I may have taken the naltrexone before, but if it was available in a pill form, I'm almost certain I've tried it before. With a shot, it's not like you can un-take it, so I think that would work better for me.
Doctor: Has the patient ever experienced any adverse effects or lack of efficacy with naltrexone in pill form? Additionally, is there a history of liver disease or any other contraindications to naltrexone/Vivitrol?
Patient: I don't remember having any bad side effects from the pill form, but I'm not sure if it worked for me or not. I don't have any liver disease or other issues that would stop me from taking it.
Doctor: Thank you for sharing that. To better understand your situation, could you tell me how long you've been drinking alcohol in this pattern, and have you ever experienced any withdrawal symptoms when you've tried to cut back?
Patient: I've been drinking this way for a long time, maybe even years. I haven't had any big withdrawal symptoms when I've tried to cut back, but I do have a strong urge to drink, especially when I'm stressed or just going through my day. That's why I'm hoping the shot will help me with the cravings.
Doctor: Thank you for sharing that. To better understand your situation, could you tell me how long you've been drinking four to five times a week, and have you ever sought professional help for your alcohol use before?
Patient: I've been drinking four to five times a week for a long time, maybe even years. I haven't sought professional help before, but I know it's something I need to work on, especially with my blood pressure and overall health. That's why I'm hoping the shot will help me with the cravings.
Doctor: Thank you for sharing that. I understand this is a challenging situation, and it's great that you're seeking help. To better support you, could you tell me how long you've been drinking this way and whether you've ever sought professional help for your alcohol use before?
Patient: I've been drinking four to five times a week for a long time, maybe even years. I haven't sought professional help before, but I know it's something I need to work on, especially with my blood pressure and overall health. That's why I'm hoping the shot will help me with the cravings.
